description: Black-box view of the lab from VM 310: can each service, DNS server, and host actually be reached, and how long do the certificates have left. Everything here is probed from outside the service, so a green row means a real client would succeed. HTTPS names must match the NPM proxy hosts on VM 300 exactly - a name that only resolves through the wildcard fails TLS SNI and looks like an outage.

panels.description: Current result of every Blackbox probe: 1 means reachable, 0 means failing. This is an instant query on purpose, so a target that is removed from the scrape list disappears immediately instead of leaving a stale red 0 on screen for the rest of the dashboard time range.
panels.title: Probe status

panels.description: Total time for each probe, covering DNS resolution, TCP connect, TLS handshake, and the response. Use the phase breakdown below to attribute a slow probe to a specific layer.
panels.title: Probe duration

panels.description: Time left on each certificate. The lab hostnames share the DNS-01 wildcard certificate for *.lab.example.com, so they renew together and move as one line; yellow is under 30 days and red is under 14. The three 192.168.0.x:8006 entries are the Proxmox nodes' own self-signed certificates and are expected to sit years out.
panels.title: TLS days remaining

panels.description: Current percentage of successful probes grouped by probe class.
panels.title: Probe health by type

panels.description: Latest status code returned by each HTTP or HTTPS endpoint.
panels.title: HTTP status codes

panels.description: Split-horizon DNS query success reported by Blackbox Exporter.
panels.title: DNS query status

panels.description: Blackbox timing split into resolve, connect, TLS, processing, and transfer. A jump confined to one phase points at that layer - for example a rising TLS phase with flat processing is a handshake problem, not a slow application.
panels.title: HTTP phase duration

panels.description: Response time of the split-horizon DNS probes against the Synology resolver (192.168.0.20) and the the router (192.168.0.1). Both must answer for internal names to work.
panels.title: DNS duration

panels.description: Ping round-trip time to the core hosts. A series that stops entirely means the host went away, while a rising line means the network path degraded.
panels.title: ICMP duration

title: Availability, DNS, and TLS
